newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil traders say talk of key report just rumor.
newsitem.headline: Brazil traders say talk of key report just rumor.

text.p: Brazilian traders said they heard talk last week of an eagerly awaited forecast for Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop by a former U.S. Agriculture Department representative, but no one has been able to confirm it so far.
Former USDA representative Leon Yallouz said at a coffee seminar in Rio de Janeiro last week that he would not publish his final crop estimate until March.
But a report on Thursday reported a trader as saying the preliminary estimate was for 27 million 60-kg bags, based on field trips made in September.

"That figure was circulating last week but I asked (Yallouz) and he said, 'No I don't have this, I am travelling to the interior after the seminar and I will only have a forecast in March'," said Francisco Ourique, one of the organisers of the seminar.
"For anyone who deals in coffee, they know that making a forecast for the 1997/98 crop in September is impossible," he added.
Yallouz was unavailable for comment Thursday.
Other traders said they had heard rumors about the preliminary forecast as far back as December, but added that no fresh talk emerged today.

"I heard rumors about the forecast in December," said the head of forecasting at a major trade house. "But when somebody talked about 27 million bags, no one could confirm if it was for 1996/97 or for 1997/98."
"It was a rumor without foundation," he said. "If there's been any repercussion today I haven't seen it."

The head of the primary commodities department at Brazil's Industry and Commerce Ministry last week reiterated the government was working with a range of 18 to 20 million bags, down from a 1996/97 crop of 25 million bags.
In light of this, a forecast of 27 million bags seemed slightly high, said another trader.
"There were some comments during the seminar but I didn't hear a number mentioned," he said. "But I haven't seen anything today."
